title: Lenvatinib: differentiated thyroid cancer
indication_text: Progressive, locally advanced or metastatic differentiated thyroid cancer that is refractory to radioactive iodine.
purpose: This treatment aims to slow cancer growth and help control symptoms. Your team explains the expected benefit, uncertainty and alternatives for your situation.
schedule_summary: Lenvatinib 24 mg once daily, continuously, until progression or unacceptable side effects. The clinician may prescribe a lower starting dose or later reductions.
administration_text: Take at about the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow capsules whole with water; do not crush or break them. A pharmacist can teach suspension preparation: place up to 5 whole capsules in a small container or 20 mL oral syringe, add 3 mL water, apple juice or milk, wait 10 minutes, then stir or shake for 3 minutes. Take all the mixture, add another 2 mL liquid and take the rinse. For a feeding tube use water only. If a missed dose cannot be taken within 12 hours, skip it and take the next dose at the usual time.
monitoring_summary: Every 28 days: blood count, kidney tests, coagulation, urine protein and thyroid-stimulating hormone. Liver tests every 2 weeks for the first 2 months, then monthly; calcium monthly. Blood pressure after week 1, every 2 weeks in the first 2 months, then monthly. ECG when clinically indicated.

agents.name: Lenvatinib
agents.mechanism: Blocks tumour growth and blood-vessel signals
agents.explanation: Lenvatinib blocks several signalling enzymes, including VEGF and FGF receptors, which support tumour blood vessels and growth. Effects on normal blood vessels explain why blood pressure, urine protein, bleeding and healing need attention.
agents.watch: Treat diarrhoea and vomiting promptly using the agreed plan because dehydration can damage the kidneys. Check blood pressure as taught. Report sudden severe headache, vision changes, bleeding, chest pain, severe abdominal pain or fluid leakage from an abnormal opening urgently.
risks: High blood pressure; rare hypertensive crisis
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, reduced appetite and weight loss
Protein in urine and kidney injury, especially with dehydration
Thyroid hormone changes, low calcium and liver injury
Bleeding, arterial clots, heart failure and heart-rhythm changes
Rare bowel perforation or fistula, impaired healing and neurological symptoms

Report ulcers, pain, dry mouth, difficulty swallowing or weight loss early. Ask for oral care, dietetic and swallowing support.
Follow prescribed heart and blood-pressure checks. Chest pain, fainting, palpitations or new breathlessness needs urgent advice.
New cough or breathlessness needs prompt review; serious causes include infection or lung injury.
Use prescribed support. Report persistent diarrhoea or vomiting, inability to drink, blood or severe abdominal pain.
Report reduced urine, swelling or poor fluid intake; keep blood and urine tests.
Report painful palms or soles, rash or blistering early. Severe spreading rash or mouth/eye involvement needs urgent review.
Discuss fertility preservation, contraception, pregnancy and breastfeeding before starting.

evidence.title: What the evidence can tell you
evidence.intro: Research supports a treatment discussion; it cannot predict one person’s outcome.
evidence.population: Progressive, locally advanced or metastatic differentiated thyroid cancer that is refractory to radioactive iodine.
evidence.comparison: Placebo in the cited randomised trial
evidence.interpretation: SELECT randomised 392 people with radioactive-iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer to lenvatinib or placebo. Median progression-free survival was 18.3 versus 3.6 months (hazard ratio 0.21; 99% CI 0.14–0.31). This endpoint is time to progression or death. The trial does not establish that an individual will live an extra 14.7 months, and its results cannot directly rank lenvatinib against sorafenib in a different trial.
limitations: Trial populations and schedules differ; comparisons across separate trials are unreliable.
An improvement in progression-free survival is not automatically an overall-survival benefit.
